extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff; USPTO disciplinary decisionmakers
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition, stay, probation, notice, and enforcement of reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when a practitioner has been disciplined by a state authority. Explains service, response deadlines, Order-to-Show-Cause process, publication, and related regulatory citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director may impose reciprocal discipline (e.g., suspension) identical to that imposed by another duly constituted authority (here, a state court's probated suspension) pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order applies the state-agreed judgment as the basis for a USPTO suspension (12 months) and places the practitioner on probation, with the suspension stayed. Action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to show a genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent seeks to contest imposition of the stayed suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the respondent must file a response within the prescribed time containing all information believed sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order directed that the response must be filed within 40 days and must contain all information the respondent believes sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted based on grounds permissible under § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice methods (mailing and publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices are to be mailed by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the address of record furnished pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11; if mailing is returned unclaimed, service by publication in the Official Gazette pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24(b) and 11.35(b) is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed to the respondent's PO box and returned 'unclaimed'; service by publication in the Official Gazette (with specified publication dates) was used to notify the respondent that he may obtain a copy by written request to the USPTO General Counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response and deadline periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific statutory/regulatory deadlines apply: the respondent had 40 days to respond to the Notice and Order; if an Order to Show Cause is issued during probation, the respondent is granted 15 days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order specified a 40-day response period for contesting imposition; the OED Director must grant 15 days to respond to an Order to Show Cause issued for alleged probation violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms and effects of a stayed suspension and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may order suspension (here, 12 months) but immediately stay the suspension and place the respondent on probation for an equal period; the respondent is permitted to practice before the Office during probation unless the stay is lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the stay is not lifted by the end of the probationary period, the respondent is not required to serve the suspension. The stay remains in effect until further order of the USPTO Director or his designate.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED procedure when respondent allegedly violates probation
rubrics_metrics.description: If, during the probationary period, the OED Director believes the respondent failed to comply with any Disciplinary Rule of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to respondent at the last address of record, and grant 15 days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the 15-day response period, if the OED Director remains of the opinion respondent violated a rule, the OED Director must deliver to the USPTO Director: (a) the Order to Show Cause, (b) respondent's response (if any), and (c) evidence supporting the opinion, and request that the USPTO Director immediately lift the stay and suspend respondent for up to twelve months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of lifting the stay and review limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director or his designate lifts the stay of suspension and respondent seeks review of that decision, the review shall not postpone or hold in abeyance the immediate suspension or other disciplinary sanction imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lifting the stay triggers immediate enforcement of suspension/sanctions regardless of any subsequent review petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inapplicability of §§ 11.58 and 11.60 unless stay lifted
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60 (procedural provisions referenced in the Order) do not apply unless the stay of the suspension is lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits which procedural protections or processes are available while the stay remains in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and dissemination of discipline per § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice of stayed suspension in the Official Gazette and give notice of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the full text of the Official Gazette 'NOTICE OF STAYED SUSPENSION' specifying the practitioner's name, registration number, suspension term and stay, probation period, the rule violated (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)), summary of the state proceedings, and a link to OED Reading Room for disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of authority to seek further discipline under §§ 11.34–11.57
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Final Order prevents the Office from seeking discipline against the respondent in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34 through 11.57 for the misconduct that caused the stay of suspension to be lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where a stayed suspension is ordered, the Office retains its broader disciplinary powers to pursue additional or alternative proceedings for underlying misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service and address-of-record requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of orders and notices must be mailed to the respondent at the most recent address provided to OED pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11; the Final Order includes a Certificate of Service attesting to mailing by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Certificate of Service specifies the respondent's law firm PO Box address and the date mailed; mailing procedures and reliance on the address-of-record are emphasized for due process and service validity.
